procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
SUI 195 was represented by Augustin Hayaz.
USA 333 was represented by Maxwell Weaver.
facts: Both boats were sailing downwind on port, towards the leeward gate mark to be rounded to port. SUI 195 was 1 boat length beyond the port lay line, sailing faster, and USA 333 was on the lay line to the mark.
When SUI 195 was 3 boat lengths from the mark, USA 333 was clear astern.
When SUI 195 was 2 boat lengths from the mark, she dropped her spinnaker and slowed down.
Shortly after, USA 333, now sailing faster, became overlapped to windward.
When at the mark, SUI 195 began to head up. Contact occurred between the starboard bow of USA 333 and midships of the port hull of SUI 195.
The damage to SUI 195 allowed water into the hull. There are multiple scuff marks on the port side of SUI 195's hull as well.
conclusions: USA 333 to windward failed to keep clear of SUI 195 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
USA 333, not overlapped with SUI 195 and not in the zone at the time SUI reached the zone, failed to give SUI mark- room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(2).
USA 333 did not avoid contact with SUI 195 when it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

It was not reasonably possible for SUI 195, the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, to avoid contact with USA 333 when it became clear that USA 333 was not giving mark-room. SUI did not break RRS 14(a).
